title: Browser, Frontend, CDN, and Edge Architecture

weeks.focus: Model browser work, route rendering, cache authority, accessibility, telemetry, and performance budgets; freeze predictions
Build and verify static, streaming, client-rendered, and private personalized storefront routes
Break and measure main-thread, hydration, memory, third-party, cache, edge, and constrained-network failures
Decide per-route architecture, defend ownership and edge limits, assess, teach, and remediate

readiness_note: Ready on 2026-08-03 after the pinned browser lab, eight paired failures, accessibility and manual checks, six isolated evaluator runs, deterministic calibration checking, semantic and resource reviews, and focused and full-course validation passed.

outcomes.statement: Trace tasks, microtasks, input dispatch, style, layout, paint, raster, and compositing from browser evidence.
Calculate route-level performance budgets and interpret controlled-lab and field evidence without conflating them.
Select and implement static, server, streaming, client, and island-hydration strategies per route from workload and interaction evidence.
Implement HTTP and CDN cache keys, freshness, validation, invalidation, and private-response isolation with explicit authority.
Build keyboard-complete, accessible, resilient interactions and explain the boundary between automated and manual evidence.
Diagnose long tasks, hydration mismatches, retained browser resources, and third-party failures from controlled evidence.
Preserve privacy-aware trace context across browser, edge, and origin while bounding telemetry cost and trust.
Defend frontend boundaries, BFF and microfrontend choices, edge consistency, ownership, cost, migration, and reversal conditions.

resources.title: HTML Living Standard: Event loops
resources.purpose: Ground tasks, microtasks, rendering opportunities, and agent event loops in the platform contract.
resources.assignment: Read definitions, queuing tasks, and the processing model; trace one input through task, microtask checkpoint, and rendering opportunity.

resources.title: RenderingNG architecture
resources.purpose: Connect style, layout, paint, raster, compositing, and thread placement to observed work.
resources.assignment: Read the pipeline and threading sections; label which Northstar work must use the main thread and which may bypass it.

resources.title: Interaction to Next Paint (INP)
resources.purpose: Interpret interaction latency and separate field thresholds from controlled lab observations.
resources.assignment: Read through the interaction anatomy and thresholds; map input delay, processing, and presentation delay to the Northstar filter interaction.

resources.title: RFC 9111: HTTP Caching
resources.purpose: Reason precisely about cache storage, freshness, validation, invalidation, and shared-cache restrictions.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 3–5 and 7; produce the cache decision table for all four Northstar routes.

resources.title: renderToPipeableStream
resources.purpose: Expose streaming HTML shell, readiness, error, and abort semantics without a framework abstraction.
resources.assignment: Read reference, caveats, and error recovery; identify when response status and headers become irreversible.

resources.title: hydrateRoot
resources.purpose: Define hydration identity, mismatch handling, and root ownership.
resources.assignment: Read caveats and error hooks; define the server/client inputs whose equality the lab must preserve.

resources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
resources.purpose: Tie resilient interaction to testable accessibility outcomes rather than tool scores.
resources.assignment: Read Principles, Conformance, 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.5.8, 3.3.1, and 4.1.2; create manual and automated checks.

resources.title: Fix memory problems
resources.purpose: Use heap growth, detached DOM, and allocation evidence to diagnose retained browser resources.
resources.assignment: Read the overview and leak workflow; define a repeated-navigation test and the evidence that distinguishes growth from a leak.

resources.title: Trace Context
resources.purpose: Propagate interoperable trace identity without trusting client sampling or leaking session data.
resources.assignment: Read the design overview and security considerations; trace browser, edge, and origin parentage and list rejected sensitive attributes.

resources.title: Life of a Pixel (Chromium University 2020)
resources.purpose: Visualize the journey from web content to displayed pixels while identifying version-bound Chromium details.
resources.assignment: Watch with captions; draw the pipeline, then annotate at least two details superseded or clarified by current RenderingNG documentation.

resources.title: Building a better web: A faster YouTube
resources.purpose: Examine how a large operator connected constrained devices, field data, code delivery, and product outcomes.
resources.assignment: Read the full case; separate measurements, interventions, product outcomes, and claims that do not transfer to Northstar.

resources.title: Browser instrumentation
resources.purpose: Inspect a browser tracing implementation while preserving its documented experimental boundary.
resources.assignment: Read the warning, setup, and instrumentation sections; record which contracts are standard and which library behavior remains experimental.

resources.title: Load Third-Party JavaScript
resources.purpose: Treat third-party code as a performance, privacy, security, and ownership dependency.
resources.assignment: Read risks, measurement, loading, and safety sections; write a Northstar admission, failure, and removal policy.

failure_experiments.scenario: long main-thread task blocks a critical interaction and next paint
failure_experiments.evidence: shared input hash, task attribution, input/processing/presentation timing, repaired yield points, and I01

failure_experiments.scenario: server and client state produce a hydration mismatch
failure_experiments.evidence: server state hash, client state hash, recoverable error, semantic DOM result, repair, and I03

failure_experiments.scenario: listeners, timers, or detached DOM survive repeated navigation
failure_experiments.evidence: navigation count, listener/timer identities, detached nodes, heap/resource delta, cleanup, and I04

failure_experiments.scenario: slow or failed third-party script blocks or breaks the core journey
failure_experiments.evidence: dependency identity, loading policy, blocked time, failure mode, fallback, owner, and I07

failure_experiments.scenario: incomplete public cache key returns the wrong regional representation
failure_experiments.evidence: normalized request dimensions, cache key, hit source, content version, region, repair, and I05

failure_experiments.scenario: shared cache stores or serves a stale personalized staff response
failure_experiments.evidence: two pseudonymous sessions, response policy, cache decision, subject binding, content version, and I06

failure_experiments.scenario: edge-origin failure serves unsafe stale data or lacks bounded degradation
failure_experiments.evidence: route authority, origin state, object age, stale policy, degraded marker, fail-closed result, and I08

failure_experiments.scenario: constrained network and device conditions violate the critical-route budget
failure_experiments.evidence: network/device profile, critical bytes and requests, route milestones, interaction result, repair, and I02
